headline: LGUs Suspend In-Person Classes on August 14 as Habagat Persists
seoTitle: August 14 Class Suspensions as Habagat Persists | FMB News
seoDescription: LGUs in NCR, Benguet, Cavite, Pangasinan and Pampanga suspended or shifted in-person classes on August 14 as the southwest monsoon continued.
deck: LGUs in NCR, Benguet, Cavite, Pangasinan and Pampanga suspended or shifted in-person classes on August 14 as the southwest monsoon continued.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Local governments in parts of Luzon suspended classes or face-to-face instruction for Friday, August 14, because of bad weather associated with the southwest monsoon.

As of GMA News Online's 6:03 a.m. update, affected areas included Malabon, Mandaluyong, Manila, Pasig and Valenzuela in Metro Manila; several towns in Benguet and Cavite; Lingayen, Mangaldan and Mangatarem in Pangasinan; and selected areas or schools in Pampanga.

Coverage differed by locality. Some declarations applied to all levels in public and private schools, while others covered specific grade levels, public schools only, selected campuses, or a shift away from face-to-face classes. Families should check the linked official list and their LGU or school announcement for the exact scope.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA's 4 a.m. forecast said the southwest monsoon was affecting Luzon and the western section of the Visayas. It forecast occasional rain over Zambales and Bataan and scattered rain and thunderstorms over Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, the Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, the rest of Central Luzon and Antique.
The weather bureau warned of possible flash floods or landslides where moderate to heavy rain occurs.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Class-suspension information changes quickly and directly affects travel, childcare and school operations. Exact grade-level and school coverage matters because not every declaration is province-wide or applicable to all institutions.
The updated list corrects the bulletin's broader description and avoids presenting unconfirmed municipalities as suspended.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Students, parents and personnel should continue monitoring their LGU, school and verified news advisories because declarations may be expanded, narrowed or lifted as local conditions change.
PAGASA advisories remain the authoritative source for the evolving rainfall and flood-risk outlook.
